It is about trusting the strength of the Savior who loved you, gave Himself for you, and is faithful to complete the work He has begun.
“And I am sure that God, who began the good work within you, will continue his work until it is finally finished on that day when Christ Jesus comes back again.” (Philippians 1:6).
Conclusion
Strongholds vs. Sins
Strongholds are lies believed as truth.
All you have to do is open the door, and a stronghold can begin to form (even with your thoughts)
The battlefield is the mind before it is the behavior.
All Satan needs is to start wearing on your mind little by little, and over time, the truth drifts (use aviation, SOP drift)
Truth from God's Word tears down lies.
From all books of the Bible, Old and New Testament, repeatedly, Jesus tells us how to win this war
Jesus is the source of real freedom.
Trust in Jesus for the win
Biblical discipleship and accountability are God's design for lasting change.
You cannot do this alone; you need a band of brothers and sisters in Christ to keep you accountable.

These evil desires lead to evil actions, and evil actions lead to death.”

You must warn each other every day, as long as it is called "today," so that none of you will be deceived by sin and hardened against God.”
John 8:34–36 (NLT) — “Jesus replied, "I assure you that everyone who sins is a slave of sin.
A slave is not a permanent member of the family, but a son is part of the family forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you will indeed be free.”
Ephesians 6:10–18 (NLT) — “A final word: Be strong with the Lord's mighty power.
Put on all of God's armor so that you will be able to stand firm against all strategies and tricks of the Devil.
For we are not fighting against people made of flesh and blood, but against the evil rulers and authorities of the unseen world, against those mighty powers of darkness who rule this world, and against wicked spirits in the heavenly realms.
Use every piece of God's armor to resist the enemy in the time of evil, so that after the battle you will still be standing firm.
Stand your ground, putting on the sturdy belt of truth and the body armor of God's righteousness.
For shoes, put on the peace that comes from the Good News, so that you will be fully prepared.

Pray at all times and on every occasion in the power of the Holy Spirit. Stay alert and be persistent in your prayers for all Christians everywhere.”

title: The Dark Room
content:
The Dark Room
The Disciple Code
2 Corinthians 4:3–4 "If the Good News we preach is hidden behind a veil, it is hidden only from people who are perishing. Satan, who is the god of this world, has blinded the minds of those who don't believe."
John 3:3 "I tell you the truth, unless you are born again, you cannot see the Kingdom of God."
Ephesians 2:4–5 "But God is so rich in mercy, and he loved us so much, that even though we were dead because of our sins, he gave us life when he raised Christ from the dead."
Ephesians 2:10 “For we are God's masterpiece. He has created us anew in Christ Jesus, so that we can do the good things he planned for us long ago.”
How God Shapes a Man Before He Uses Him
Every Disciple Begins the Same Way
Every man who belongs to Jesus Christ has one thing in common. Before God changed the direction of his life, He changed the direction of his eyes. The greatest miracle in a believer's life is not that he decided to follow Christ, but that God graciously opened his eyes to see Christ. Until that moment, the Gospel could be heard without being understood, read without being believed, and explained without being treasured.
2 Corinthians 4:3–4 says, "If the Good News we preach is hidden behind a veil, it is hidden only from people who are perishing. Satan, who is the god of this world, has blinded the minds of those who don't believe." Spiritual blindness is not merely ignorance. It is the inability to see the glory of Jesus Christ apart from the work of God.
The Greatest Miracle Is Learning to See
Many people assume becoming a Christian simply means changing beliefs or adopting better morals. The Bible will teach you that it is much more than that.
John 3:3 "I tell you the truth, unless you are born again, you cannot see the Kingdom of God." Jesus did not first speak about entering the Kingdom. He spoke about seeing it. Before anyone can follow Christ, God must awaken a heart that is spiritually dead and open eyes that are spiritually blind.
Ephesians 2:4–5 "But God is so rich in mercy, and he loved us so much, that even though we were dead because of our sins, he gave us life when he raised Christ from the dead."
Salvation begins with God. Dead men do not revive themselves, and blind men do not restore their own sight. The grace that saves us is the same grace that enables us to see the beauty and sufficiency of Jesus Christ.
The Cross
The moment a person places his faith in Jesus Christ, the entire direction of his life changes. He is no longer trusting his own goodness but the perfect righteousness of Christ.
Ephesians 2:8–9 "God saved you by his grace when you believed. And you can't take credit for this; it is a gift from God. Salvation is not a reward for the good things we have done."
The cross is no longer simply a historical event. It becomes intensely personal. Christ did not merely die for sinners; He died for me. His righteousness becomes my righteousness. His sacrifice satisfies God's justice on my behalf. Every lesson that follows in the Christian life begins here, because until a man understands what Jesus accomplished on the cross, he will spend the rest of his life trying to earn what God has already freely given through His Son.
Growing Christians See More of God's Holiness
Many people assume that spiritual maturity is measured by how much Bible knowledge a person has accumulated or how many years he has been a Christian. The Bible points to a different measurement. As believers walk with Christ, they begin to see God more clearly than ever before. His holiness becomes more than a theological word. It becomes a reality that reshapes the heart.
Isaiah 6:3 records the angels continually crying, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Heaven's Armies. The whole earth is filled with his glory!" They never grow tired of declaring His holiness because His holiness is infinite.
Revelation 4:8 "Day after day and night after night they keep on saying, 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty.'" Heaven is captivated by the holiness of God because there is nothing and no one like Him.
Jesus is no longer viewed merely as a compassionate teacher or an inspiring example. He is the eternal Son of God, worthy of worship.
Hebrews 1:3 "The Son radiates God's own glory and expresses the very character of God."
Colossians 1:15–17 "Christ is the visible image of the invisible God... He existed before anything else, and he holds all creation together."
The longer a disciple walks with Christ, the more he realizes that the One who welcomed children, healed the sick, and forgave sinners is also the Lord before whom angels veil their faces. A growing knowledge of God's holiness produces greater reverence, deeper worship, and increasing awe. He is infinitely greater than we first imagined.
Growing Christians Also See More of Their Own Sin
At first this truth seems backwards. Many people expect that as they mature in Christ they will think less about sin because they are becoming more obedient. As the light of God's holiness shines more brightly into our lives, it exposes areas of the heart that we never recognized before.
Jeremiah 17:9 "The human heart is the most deceitful of all things, and desperately wicked."  We often see the outward sins first, but the Holy Spirit patiently reveals the pride, selfish ambition, envy, unbelief, fear, and love of self that remain beneath the surface. Growth in holiness is not pretending those sins no longer exist. It is allowing God to expose them so they can be confessed and forsaken.
When Isaiah saw the Lord seated upon His throne, his first response was not confidence but confession.
Isaiah 6:5 "Then I said, 'It's all over! I am doomed, for I am a sinful man.'" The closer he came to God's holiness, the more clearly, he saw his own need for mercy. Spiritual maturity is not thinking that you have become a better person than everyone else. It is becoming increasingly aware that apart from Christ you have nothing to boast about. This awareness does not produce hopelessness because the Gospel continually points to the sufficiency of Jesus Christ. Conviction is one of God's greatest acts of grace because He only exposes what He intends to heal.
The Cross Gets Bigger Every Year
As a believer grows in the knowledge of God's holiness and becomes increasingly aware of his own sinfulness, the cross becomes larger, not because Christ's sacrifice changes, but because the believer finally begins to understand what it truly accomplished.
Romans 5:8 "But God showed his great love for us by sending Christ to die for us while we were still sinners."
2 Corinthians 5:21 "For God made Christ, who never sinned, to be the offering for our sin, so that we could be made right with God through Christ." Those verses become richer every year because we see more clearly both the depth of our need and the greatness of God's grace.
The Gospel is the foundation beneath every step of the Christian life. The more clearly, we understand our own sin, the more we treasure the mercy of God. The more we understand His holiness, the more astonishing His grace becomes.
Galatians 6:14 "As for me, may I never boast about anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ."
Every victory over sin, every act of obedience, every step of spiritual growth, and every hope of eternal life rests upon the same unchanging truth: Jesus Christ accomplished on the cross what no man could ever accomplish for himself. The mature disciple never graduates from the cross. He spends the rest of his life standing in its shadow, worshipping the Savior who loved him and gave Himself for him.
God Is Preparing You for What He Has Prepared for You
Waiting is one of the hardest classrooms in the Christian life because it requires us to trust what we cannot yet see. We naturally measure progress by visible results, but God measures progress by spiritual maturity. Before He entrusts greater responsibility, He develops greater character. Before He enlarges our influence, He deepens our dependence upon Him. The waiting season is not evidence that God has forgotten His promises. More often, it is evidence that He is faithfully preparing His servant to carry those promises well.
Isaiah 40:31 “But those who wait on the LORD will find new strength. They will fly high on wings like eagles. They will run and not grow weary. They will walk and not faint.”, this reminds us that God's strength is given to those who learn to wait upon Him rather than run ahead of Him.
The temptation during these seasons is to believe that nothing is happening because nothing is visible. While Joseph sat in an Egyptian prison, God was preparing a ruler. While David fled from Saul, God was preparing a king. While Moses cared for sheep in Midian, God was preparing a deliverer. None of those men could see what God was doing, but every ordinary day was shaping them for an extraordinary calling.
Romans 8:28 — “And we know that God causes everything to work together for the good of those who love God and are called according to his purpose for them.” reminds believers that God is continually working, even when His work remains hidden from our eyes.
The Danger of Running Ahead of God
One of the greatest dangers for any disciple is confusing God's calling with God's timing. It is possible to know what God has called you to do while still needing to wait for His appointed time. Throughout Scripture, impatience repeatedly led God's people into unnecessary pain. Abraham attempted to fulfill God's promise through Hagar instead of waiting for Isaac. Saul refused to wait for Samuel and offered a sacrifice he had no authority to offer. Israel repeatedly acted out of fear instead of trusting God's timing. Their problem was rarely that they doubted God's power. They doubted His timetable.
God's timing is never accidental. Ecclesiastes 3:11 — “God has made everything beautiful for its own time. He has planted eternity in the human heart, but even so, people cannot see the whole scope of God's work from beginning to end.” He makes everything beautiful in its time, not ours. Waiting often exposes what we truly trust. Do we trust God's promises only when they arrive quickly, or do we trust His character even when the answer seems delayed? Faith continues obeying when sight offers no immediate reward.
The Dark Room Produces Men Who Last
A photographer understands that an image is developed in darkness before it is ever displayed in the light. If the photograph is exposed too early, the image is ruined. The illustration is not found directly in Scripture, but it beautifully describes a biblical principle that appears throughout God's Word. God repeatedly develops His servants in hidden places before placing them in visible ones. The wilderness came before the Promised Land. The shepherd's field came before the throne. The prison came before the palace. The cross came before the resurrection. God has never been in a hurry because He is preparing people for eternity, not simply for temporary success.
If you find yourself living in what feels like the white space of your story, do not assume God has stopped writing. The pages that seem empty to you may be the chapters where He is accomplishing His greatest work.
Philippians 1:6 —" And I am sure that God, who began the good work within you, will continue his work until it is finally finished on that day when Christ Jesus comes back again.” Every believer can be assured that the God who began His work will faithfully complete it. The waiting season is not where God's plan pauses. It is often where His plan takes its deepest root. When the day comes that He opens the next door, you will discover that the years you thought were empty were the years that prepared you for everything He had planned all along.
Conclusion
The Story Is Not Finished Yet
Every disciple eventually finds himself in one of two places. Either God is clearly opening doors, or He seems to be asking you to wait. The Bible teaches that both seasons are equally important. We often celebrate the moments when God is visibly working, but Scripture repeatedly reminds us that some of His greatest work is accomplished long before anyone else can see it. The years spent in obscurity, the prayers that seem unanswered, the opportunities that have not yet arrived, and the promises that have not yet been fulfilled are never outside of God's sovereign care. The Lord who calls His people is also the Lord who prepares them.
The pattern appears throughout the entire Bible. Even Jesus lived in relative obscurity before beginning His public ministry. None of those years were wasted because God's purpose was never simply to prepare a position. He was preparing the person who would one day stand in that position.
Romans 8:28 — “And we know that God causes everything to work together for the good of those who love God and are called according to his purpose for them.”
The same pattern is seen in the life of Paul. His conversion was immediate, but his preparation was not. The Lord gave him spiritual sight before He entrusted him with spiritual leadership. He learned the greatness of God's holiness, the depth of his own sin, the sufficiency of Christ's grace, and the necessity of patiently waiting upon God's timing. Those hidden years became the foundation upon which the rest of his ministry would stand.
Perhaps you find yourself living in that same season today. You know God has saved you. You desire to serve Him faithfully. Yet it feels as though your life has entered a chapter where little seems to be happening. The temptation is to believe that God has forgotten you or that His promises have somehow failed. Scripture tells a different story. The white space is not empty. The waiting is not meaningless. The silence is not evidence of God's absence. More often, it is evidence that He is patiently accomplishing a work that cannot yet be seen.
James 1:2–4 — “Dear brothers and sisters, whenever trouble comes your way, let it be an opportunity for joy.”
Isaiah 40:31 — “But those who wait on the LORD will find new strength. They will fly high on wings like eagles. They will run and not grow weary. They will walk and not faint.”
The disciple who understands these truths no longer measures God's faithfulness by how quickly prayers are answered or doors are opened. He measures God's faithfulness by the cross of Jesus Christ, where God's love, wisdom, holiness, mercy, and promises were displayed forever.
Philippians 1:6 — “And I am sure that God, who began the good work within you, will continue his work until it is finally finished on that day when Christ Jesus comes back again.”
The dark room will not last forever. When God's work of preparation is complete, He will accomplish His purposes in His perfect time. Until then, remain faithful, remain in His Word, remain in prayer, and remember that God is always preparing His people for what He has already prepared for them.
